=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): opposite (clearly visible as paired leaves emerging from the same nodes along the stem in all images)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): distal (leaves are spaced apart along the elongated stem rather than grouped together)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3.	Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (leaves consist of a single blade without division into leaflets)
    4.	Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5.	Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6.	Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A
C. Leaf Morphology
    7.	Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): entire (margins appear smooth, though some leaves show holes due to damage)
    8.	Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): ovate to elliptic (broadest near the base, tapering towards the apex; shape varies slightly between juvenile and mature leaves)
    9.	Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acuminate (tapers to a distinct, elongated point)
    10.	Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): rounded to cordate (base is generally rounded, with some leaves showing a slight heart-shaped indentation)
    11.	Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (single midrib with lateral veins branching off)
    12.	Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): clearly visible, curved, and arranged in multiple pairs arching towards the leaf margin (arcuate)
    13.	Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny (leaves reflect light, indicating a smooth, somewhat glossy surface)
    14.	Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs on the leaf surface)
    15.	Petiole length (short / long): long (petioles are slender and noticeably elongated relative to the leaf blade)
    16.	Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (petioles appear round in cross-section and smooth)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17.	Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): herbaceous (stem appears green, slender, and flexible, typical of a vine or herbaceous seedling)
    18.	Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (stem surface appears smooth)
    19.	Stem color: green (uniformly green throughout the visible sections)
    20.	Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (no visible ridges or rough texture)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21.	Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no distinct stipules observed at the leaf bases)
    22.	Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed
    23.	Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent
    24.	Tendrils (present / absent): absent
F. Notes: Several leaves exhibit irregular holes and missing tissue along the margins. The plant appears to be a climbing vine or a scrambling seedling given the long petioles and slender stem structure. Juvenile leaves appear more rounded, while mature leaves are more elongated.
